choices.text: It is a new vector, because its start point moved
It is the same vector: free vectors slide
It becomes a position vector for the new point

questions.feedback: If you picked the first option, that is the trap: Moving a vector to a new start point changes it. Reteach point: Free vectors slide: the same arrow drawn anywhere is the same vector. Only position vectors are pinned to the origin.
questions.misconception: Moving a vector to a new start point changes it.
questions.prompt: A free vector is redrawn starting at a new point, with the same length and direction. Which statement is correct?

questions.feedback: Use Pythagoras on the components before reaching for a number: if you answered 14 you added the parts, and if you answered 100 you forgot the square root.
questions.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the vector (6, 8).

questions.feedback: a . b = |a||b| cos theta, so a . b = 0 means cos theta = 0 and theta = 90 degrees: the vectors are perpendicular. Parallel vectors give cos theta = 1 or -1, never 0.
questions.prompt: If a . b = 0 for two non-zero vectors a and b, what does that tell you?

questions.feedback: lambda scales the direction vector first, then adds it to the fixed point: (1, 2, 3) + (2, 0, -2) = (3, 2, 1). The point (1, 2, 3) itself is the lambda = 0 case.
questions.prompt: A line has vector equation r = (1, 2, 3) + lambda(1, 0, -1). Write down the position vector of the point on the line when lambda = 2.
